guard: the fixture waits on the auth service's own readiness signal (discovery file, pid alive, /health on the recorded URL) and an exhausted budget throws naming the auth service instead of falling through into a misattributed 502
why: #1534: the readiness loop was one hundred fetches one hundred milliseconds apart with no
assertion on exhaustion. A contended runner whose child outlived that budget got a silent
fall-through, the TLS proxy was built over a port nothing was listening on, and the first
exchange cell reported 502 !== 200 as an apparent exchange misconfiguration. The service
already had a readiness contract (the discovery file is written only after every plane is
bound); the fixture now drives it through the provider's shipped ready() with the provider's
own fifteen-second budget, and a never-ready service is a thrown error naming the service.

mutations.name: the exhausted readiness budget silently returns instead of throwing, as before the fix
mutations.find: await prepared.service.ready({ dir: serverDir, timeoutMs: AUTH_SERVICE_READY_TIMEOUT_MS });
mutations.replace: await prepared.service.ready({ dir: serverDir, timeoutMs: AUTH_SERVICE_READY_TIMEOUT_MS }).catch(() => {});
mutations.expectRed: a service that never becomes ready fails the wait loudly, naming the auth service
mutations.cell: a service that never becomes ready fails the wait loudly, naming the auth service
